system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note are not evidence of Buyer agreement. Review all positions critically. The recommendations below are Buyer negotiating positions, based only on the supplied documents—not independent verification of DD-002–DD-012.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A meaningful general warranty cap, with separate protection for higher-risk categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recourse; exclude fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud from this cap—20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, related-claim aggregation and a tipping basket; exclusions for separately protected claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related claims—the proposed combination could eliminate meaningful recovery for recurring smaller losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with distinct periods for other categories and notified claims surviving expiry. | **Seek 24 months and reject universal application**—Buyer needs adequate post-Completion discovery time without inadvertently shortening other protections. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title receive the same caps and periods as general warranties. | Separate warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issue, the entire issued capital and freedom from encumbrances. | **Seek a 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and a seven-year contractual notification period**, preserving fraud treatment—ownership risk should not be limited to AUD 4.8m or 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud exception is supplied; limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent-misrepresentation claims, including appropriate attribution to Seller representatives. | **Carve fraud out of caps, contractual time bars, thresholds, disclosure/knowledge defences, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, preserving non-excludable rights—blanket provisions must not shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure against relevant warranties, sufficiently detailed to identify the matter’s nature and scope, using an agreed frozen record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific, intelligible disclosures and an archived index**—document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; alternatively, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer deal personnel. | **Delete constructive/imputed knowledge and any duty to investigate**, with specific indemnities unaffected—“discoverable” matters would turn diligence access into a broad warranty defence. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite missing evidence of associated conditions. | A Buyer-waivable Completion condition requiring valid, effective consent and satisfaction of relevant clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable amendments. | **Do not complete until compliant consent and condition-satisfaction evidence are delivered**, with a long-stop termination right—approximately 30% of FY26 revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release follows Completion. | Debt discharged through Completion funds flow, deducted under agreed debt-free/cash-free mechanics, with effective security releases. | **Require a binding payout letter and simultaneous discharge/release arrangements, not an unsecured post-Completion promise**—Buyer should not acquire continuing secured debt exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller calls them its responsibility; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, including amounts payable after Completion. | **Expressly allocate liability to Seller and capture it in funds flow/price adjustments or a secured indemnity, without double counting**—calling bonuses a Seller matter does not prevent the Company funding them. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open; transfer conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. | Evidence that all transfer conditions are met and an effective, comprehensive assignment of relevant IP, backed by a separate indemnity. | **Require payment reconciliation, cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment before Completion; expand indemnity to ownership/use disputes, remediation and third-party losses**—paying one invoice may neither establish title nor cover resulting losses. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preserved evidence, containment and a documented legal notification assessment, plus protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation/remediation covenants and a specific indemnity for resulting liabilities and reasonable response costs, to the extent lawful**—uncertainty is not proof of immateriality, but neither is the record proof of a notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Aggregate assessment of timing, commitment, termination rights, accruals and treatment under the agreed price mechanics. | **Review all three together and require consent for material new commitments; allocate costs according to their actual character**—AUD 330,000 cannot be dismissed as ordinary course, or automatically treated as debt, without evidence. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and price/debt adjustments; fraud separately preserved. | **Create an express category-by-category limitations matrix and precedence provision**—otherwise global drafting can silently defeat negotiated protections and payment obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent corroboration of issued capital, ownership, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer requirements. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records and supporting issue/transfer documents, conduct relevant searches and obtain Completion transfer/registration deliverables**—the register is important evidence, not complete verification of unencumbered ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Separate tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity with appropriate longer survival; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Keep both open: propose seven-year tax protection with a separate cap and no general thresholds; negotiate IP-specific protection and preserve the Ironquay indemnity**—neither category should be deemed resolved by an inadequate general regime. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge arrangements, Seller-funded bonuses, and verified Ironquay IP transfer. The incident investigation and remaining diligence should inform whether further Completion conditions, holdbacks or specific indemnities are needed.
=== END ADVICE ===
